picks.title: How Can You So Brazenly Insult Past Acharyas Of Vedanta
picks.summary: “Krishna is the Supreme Person, but at the same time He is beyond the knowledge of Brahman and Paramatma. The yogis and jnanis are confused in their attempts to understand Krishna, although the greatest of the impersonalists, Shripada Shankaracharya, has admitted in his Gita commentary that Krishna is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But his followers do not accept Krishna as such, for it is very difficult to know Krishna, even though one has transcendental realization of impersonal Brahman.” (Shrila Prabhupada, Bhagavad-gita, 7.3 Purport)
picks.reason: Discusses Krishna's supreme nature and Vedanta's view on ultimate reality and knowledge.

picks.title: 1813: The Philosopher vs the Mystic | Understanding the Passion of the Gopīs
picks.summary: To the philosopher, the weeping of Krishna's lovers looks like ordinary suffering. To the mystics it's the culmination of the highest knowledge. Evelyn Underhill — first woman to lecture in theology at Oxford — said the mystic speaks the disconcerting language of first-hand experience, something only really understood by another who has felt it. Raghunath and Kaustubha explore what it means to move from thinking to tasting — and why the passion of the gopīs is where all philosophy ends. Srimad Bhagavatam 10.39.8-26   ******************************************************************** LOVE THE
picks.reason: Explores mystical passion in Krishna's devotees, a profound Hindu spiritual theme.

picks.summary:

picks.title: I Know What To Do…So Why Dont I Do It? | Pujya Snehmunidas Swami | Windows Into Wisdom
picks.summary: Why do we know what is right, but still struggle to do it? In this episode of Windows into Wisdom by BAPS Better Living, we sit down with Pujya Snehmunidas Swami to explore one of the most honest struggles in spiritual growth: the gap between knowing better and actually doing better. Many of us have heard wisdom about patience, forgiveness, discipline, prayer, humility, and inner change. picks.reason: Explores the gap between knowing dharma and practicing it, a key Hindu struggle.
